title: Many-Shot In-Context Learning in Multimodal Foundation Models

model.params_source: paper Sec. 3.1 (temperature zero and a fixed random seed for GPT-4o); seed value, max_tokens and top_p assumed

task.subset_rule: paper-defined split: the paper's own class-balanced random sample of HAM10000 (805 demo / 210 test, Table 1)
task.approximation: the demo/test sampling seed and the demo-set size at 'Best' are not in the text (Figure 7 only); queries batched 50 per request as in the paper's many-shot runs

items.source: HAM10000 (Tschandl et al. 2018), Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/DBW86T (HAM10000_images_part_1.zip 1.37 GB, HAM10000_images_part_2.zip 1.40 GB, HAM10000_metadata.tab); demo/test sets re-sampled class-balanced from the HAM10000 training data as in Sec. 3.2
items.config_or_split: none (paper-specific random split: 805 demo / 210 test, class-balanced over the 7 classes)

fields.label: dx (akiec, bcc, bkl, df, mel, nv, vasc)

placeholders.format_blocks:
for each query index qn_idx in the batch: 
Please respond with the following format for each question:
---BEGIN FORMAT TEMPLATE FOR QUESTION {qn_idx}---
Answer Choice {qn_idx}: [Your Answer Choice Here for Question {qn_idx}]
Confidence Score {qn_idx}: [Your Numerical Prediction Confidence Score Here From 0 To 1 for Question {qn_idx}]
---END FORMAT TEMPLATE FOR QUESTION {qn_idx}---
Do not deviate from the above format. Repeat the format template for the answer.
placeholders.class_desp: Python str() of the list of the 7 class names (e.g. "['actinic keratoses', 'basal cell carcinoma', ...]") as passed by the paper's code; exact class strings must be taken from the paper's code release
placeholders.demo_answer: class name of the demo image
placeholders.<<IMG>>: the image attached at that position of the message (one image part per <>)

prompt.few_shot: many-shot: N demonstration images from the 805-image demo set at the best demo-set size for HAM10000 (N is read from Figure 7, not printed in the text; the paper scales N log-linearly up to the full demo set)
prompt.source_location: Appendix A.2 (batched image-classification prompt; A.1 is the single-query form)
prompt.verbatim: partial: the f-string code of Appendix A.2 is rendered as text; the extraction's line-continuation marks ('question-\nusing', 'Here-\nFrom') were re-joined; class_desp strings are not printed

output.parse: regex 'Answer Choice (\d+): (.+)' per question in the batched reply; the answer string is matched to a class name in class_desp
output.postprocess: strip, lowercase, exact match on the class name; unparsable or missing answers count as incorrect (Sec. 3.3)

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: fraction of the 210 test images whose predicted class equals dx, at the best demo-set size
metric.original_location: Table 2, row HAM10000, column GPT-4o Best (zero-shot 34.93)

open_points: The demo-set size behind 'Best' (53.59) for HAM10000/GPT-4o is only in Figure 7 (image); read it from the PDF or the authors' code release before the run.

The 805/210 demo/test split of HAM10000 is a paper-specific random class-balanced sample whose seed is not printed; check whether the code release ships the split, otherwise draw a seeded split (seed 20260907) and treat the comparison as set-level.
Image detail level (low/high) for the ~855 images per request is not stated; with high detail the request exceeds the 128k context, so 'low' is the only feasible reading.
Exact class_desp strings (the 7 class names as passed to the prompt) must be taken from the code release.
notes: Cost is dominated by image tokens: 5 batched requests per seed, each with up to 805 demo images plus 50 queries (~73k tokens at low detail). Cheap fallback: zero-shot column (34.93) needs 5 batched calls without demos. Table 2 'Best' is the maximum over demo sizes and is optimistically biased.
